submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a word-fragment token that cannot stand as a complete word: most strongly on a bare capital-letter or short onset token (' Z', ' K', ' B', ' Ty', ' Be', ' Ly') that begins an unfamiliar name GPT-2 splits into pieces, often in a name/place slot ('Dr. Z', 'village of K', 'Sargans, Z'), and also on mid-word fragments of rarer words ('r|az|ors') and on tokens inside random alphanumeric strings (URL shortcodes, hashes, passwords). Whole-word tokens (' Smith', ' Oxford', ' Warsaw', ' apples'), ordinary prose and the first token stay near zero, so there is no floor; the response is retrospective, judged from the fragment itself before its continuation is read.
